questions.question: Which of the following winds are hot dust-laden and blow from Sahara desert towards Mediterranean Region?
questions.solution:
• **Sirocco** is a Mediterranean wind that comes from the Sahara and can reach hurricane speeds in North Africa and Southern Europe, especially during the summer season.
 
• The **Loo** is a strong, dusty, hot and dry summer wind from the west which blows over the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region of North India and Pakistan.
 
• A **Föhn or foehn** is a type of dry, warm, down-slope wind that occurs in the lee (downwind side) of a mountain range. 
 
• The **mistral** is a strong, cold, northwesterly wind that blows from southern France into the Gulf of Lion in the northern Mediterranean, with sustained winds often exceeding 66 km/h.

questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for giving color to human skin?
questions.solution: Melanin is generally a complex polymer derived from the amino acid tyrosine that is responsible for determining skin and hair color. It is seen in the skin to a certain degree, depending on how much a population has been exposed to the sun historically.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is non-communicable in nature?
questions.solution: Cancer along with chronic lung diseases, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases are few diseases that are non-communicable in nature. NCDs or non-communicable diseases are those conditions that are usually not passed on from one affected person to others but are caused as a direct result of lifestyle and environmental factors.

questions.question: Which key is used to move to next line in an MS-Word document?
questions.solution: The Enter key is used in MS-Word is used to move to the next line whereas The Shift keys combine with other keys to help in different actions.

questions.question: In which industry Potassium Nitrate is used commercially?
questions.solution: Potassium nitrate is used mainly in firecrackers manufacturing along with fertilizers, tree stump removal, and rocket propellants. The main reason is that it is the oxidizer in black powder, which is used in almost all fireworks.

questions.question: What was the main motive of Third Five Year Plan in India?

questions.question: Electric Motor converts ________ energy into mechanical energy
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Electric Motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. **__
 
• It works because of electromagnetic induction, which is when a voltage is induced by a changing magnetic field.
 
• That would make the copper coil inside the motor turn around repeatedly inside its permanent magnet.
 
• Electric motor thus makes mechanical energy through the interaction between magnetic fields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea728f908b060e4db8cdc0f37188bd8bacc49aff99cc89b07517095538ec56de.png] 

 
• Electric Generator converts Mechanical energy to Electrical energy.

questions.question: Which play of Shakespeare's was recently claimed to be dated wrongly?
questions.solution: Researchers believed that Shakespeare wrote his play Hamlet in early 1601 when Elizabeth I was still on the throne after more than 42 years. Researchers have found that this is the wrong date and that the Bard did not produce the finished version for another two years.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of Allotrope?
questions.solution: Allotropes are generally elements which exist in two or more different forms in the same physical state and they also differ in physical properties and chemical activity. Diamond, graphite, and fullerenes are three allotropes of the element carbon. Steel, on the other hand, is an alloy of iron and carbon and other elements.

questions.question: Optical fiber works on which of the following principle of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Total Internal Reflection__.

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Total Internal reflection: The total reflection of light from a higher refractive index medium to back in its medium at an angle more than a critical angle known as total internal reflection.

 
 
• It always happens when light travels from denser medium to rarer medium.
 
 

 
• Optical fibre: It is a very thin fibre made of glass and plastic having a radius of the order of a micrometre (10-6 m).

 
 
• It works on the principle of Total Internal Reflection.
 
• It is lightweight, fast, and useful for long-distance data and light transmission with very few losses.
 
• A bundle of such thin fibres forms a light pipe.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34094a0e490a9feb4659252b34c42b4112b08c0037ebde7ad1f146ceba30ac62.png] 

 
• Scattering of light: The phenomenon in which the particles in a colloid scatter the beams of light that are directed at them is called scattering of light.
 
• Refraction: When a ray of light passes from one medium to another it suffers a change in direction at the boundary of two media is called refraction.
 
• Reflection: The phenomena in which light ray is sent back into the same medium from which it is coming, on interaction with boundary, is called reflection.

EXPLANATION__:

__
 
• Optical fibres__ work on the principle of __Total Internal Reflection__.
 
• Total Internal Reflection refers to the complete reflection of a ray of light within a given medium from the surrounding surface.

questions.question: Which Sikh Guru initiated 'The Khalsa'?
questions.solution: The Khalsa is the army of all initiated Sikhs represented by the five beloved-ones and can be called the Guru Panth and was initiated on 13 April 1699, by Guru Gobind Singh who was the tenth Sikh Guru. The word Khalsa generally means "pure”.

questions.question: Which of the following three R's are regarded as environment friendly?
questions.solution:
**The 'Reduce', 'Reuse' and 'Recycle' elements are referred to as the '3 R's'.**

**Reducing **- Try to reduce the amount of waste produced, as this is the best way to help the environment.

**Reusing** – New methods must be applied for reusing all the old stuff.

**Recycling-** This enables the materials which are thrown away to be used again by making them into new products.

questions.question: Under which article, President of India can proclaim constitutional emergency?
questions.solution:
According to Article 356:

If the President, is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the Government of the State cannot be carried on by the provisions of the Constitution, the President may issue a proclamation in which the president may assume to himself all or any of the powers vested in the Governor and in such situation proclamation of Emergency is in operation, in the whole of India or in any part of the State.

questions.question: Which of the following are longest cell of the human body?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Nerve Cells__.**

**Nerve Cells:-**

 
• Nerve cells are the **longest cells in the human body. **These are cells within the nervous system and carry messages throughout the body. The longest axons in the human body are those of the sciatic nerve, which run from the base of the spinal cord to the big toe of each foot.
 
• The Length of a nerve cell is 90cm-100cm, linking the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) to other parts of the body.
 
• **Diagram of Nerve Cell:-**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a408b3f53a3d357b2e15b43b67343bd89a7051051ae23c1b53715434569ef45f.png] 

**Extra Facts:- **

**Pancreatic Cells:-**

 
• Pancreatic cells are the islets of Langerhans, which are regions of the pancreas that contain hormone-producing endocrine cells.
 
• The Pancreas serves two functions, endocrine and exocrine.

**Epithelial Cells:-**

 
• These cells come from surfaces of your body, such as skin, blood vessels, urinary tract, or organs.
 
• They protect from viruses.

**Epidermal Cells:-**

 
• These cells are thin outer layer which is present in plants, humans, animals, etc.
 
• For Example:- the epidermis of the skin, the epidermis of roots.

questions.question: An economic system combining private and state enterprise is called as _________
questions.solution:
• A mixed economy is defined as an economic system which consists of a mixture of markets and economic planning, public ownership and private ownership and free markets
 
• In a market economy decisions regarding investment, production, and distribution are guided by the price signals created by the forces of supply and demand.
 
• A centrally planned economy is an economic system in which the state or government makes economic decisions rather than made by the interaction between businessman and customers.
 
• "Private sector of the economy” which is also known as the "private economy” comprises of all the entities that aren't an agent of the Government.
